decisions.quote: In Study 1 ( n = 32), we replicated previous findings showing an asymmetrical pattern of categorization of happy and fearful faces in 6.5‐month‐old infants, and extended these findings by demonstrating that infants’ categorization did not differ when emotions were expressed by familiar (i.e., caregiver) faces.

Reference-list inclusion plus matching phenomenon is not enough to identify the exact current empirical target. The current full body remains inaccessible after the documented free publisher, repository, Wayback and fresh collaborative-browser routes. The complete Safar2012thesis is a DIFFERENT candidate report: studies1a/1b/1c and study2at8–9months, versus current two6.5month studiesN32/N34with spontaneous-preference Study2. Parent rejects its substitution or source promotion; no experiment numbering or outcome is transferred. Thus actual experiment-to-reference identity remains unknown, not a positive omission or exclusion. JSTOR/Wiley DOI aliases of Nelson papers are one work each, not extra originals.
